name: Tarquin Osei-Mäkinen
description:
Tarquin Osei-Mäkinen is a Shelf-born vocalist and multi-instrumentalist whose career spans 2205 to the present, making him one of the few Shelf artists to achieve genuine cross-tier recognition without corporate backing. His sound is built on distorted kora strings fed through industrial feedback loops, Ghanaian bell patterns played on salvaged pipe metal, and a vocal style that blends Finnish runic chant with West African griot tradition — a lineage he claims without irony as entirely his own. His performances are confrontational, physically exhausting for audiences, and deliberately staged in locations that require effort to reach: flooded sub-basements, decommissioned transit tunnels, rooftop structures with no safe egress.

His 2219 release 'Φ0.00' — distributed on hand-etched data chips sold for exactly nothing, with the stipulation that recipients must pass them on — is considered one of the defining political art objects of the decade. The album documents one year of Shelf eviction notices, corporate water-tax hearings, and augmentation debt proceedings through field recordings, witness vocal testimony, and Osei-Mäkinen's own compositions. Tier 4 and 5 listeners who encountered it through black-market channels describe it as 'the most uncomfortable thing I've ever heard,' which Osei-Mäkinen has stated was the intended effect.
creator: Tarquin Osei-Mäkinen
audience: Shelf residents, political activists, Circuit solidarity networks, Tier 3 and 4 dissidents, underground journalists
cultural_impact: Osei-Mäkinen is one of the most politically significant artists active in GLMZ, and Vantablack Media has attempted three separate content-restriction orders against 'Φ0.00,' each of which was overturned due to the album's non-digital distribution format. His name appears in corporate security watchlists as a 'cultural agitator' — a designation that has, predictably, elevated his status considerably. He is rumored to be connected to the Shelf advocacy network known as the Hollow Floor, though he has never confirmed this.
story_hooks: A Vantablack security contractor is tasked with locating Osei-Mäkinen's next illegal venue before the show — not to shut it down, but to plant a surveillance node that can identify attendees.
A Tier 4 corporate executive's teenager is found with a 'Φ0.00' chip, triggering a family crisis and a desperate attempt to locate where it came from before it reaches the wrong ears.
Osei-Mäkinen announces a 'final performance' at an undisclosed location — and the coordinates, when decoded, point to the lobby of a Vantablack subsidiary tower.
